    s = _DIGIT_HYPHEN_DIGIT_RE.sub("", s)
    s = s.replace("¥", "-").replace("¶", "-").replace("§", "-").replace("¤", "-")
    s = re.sub(r"-{2,}", "-", s)
    return s.strip("-")

    s_parts = slug_tail.split("-")

    n, m = len(s_parts), len(b_parts)

    for i in range(m - n + 1):

    return False

class SessionManager:
    """
    BIG PICTURE:
      • Create one requests.Session you reuse across all calls.
      • This gives you:
          - Reused TCP/TLS connections (keep-alive)
          - Lower latency (especially over TLS handshakes)
          - Shared headers / timeouts

    FINE DETAIL:
      • We mount a default HTTPAdapter (pool size is small; we don't parallelize).
      • We set Accept & Accept-Encoding to 'gzip' (requests decompresses for us).
      • Timeouts are per-request; tiny but safe for a single GET per action.
    """
    _session: Optional[requests.Session] = None

    @classmethod
    def get(cls) -> requests.Session:
        if cls._session is None:
            s = requests.Session()
            # Friendly, explicit headers
            s.headers.update({
                "User-Agent": DEFAULT_USER_AGENT,
                "Accept": "text/html, */*;q=0.8",
                "Accept-Encoding": "gzip, deflate",
                "Connection": "keep-alive",
            })
            # Leave default adapter; pool defaults are enough for single-thread use.
            cls._session = s
        return cls._session

def http_get(url: str, headers=None, timeout=15, allow_redirects=True) -> requests.Response:
    """
    One GET with keep-alive. We do .raise_for_status() so callers only handle success paths.
    """
    s = SessionManager.get()
    h = dict(s.headers)
    if headers:
        h.update(headers)
    r = s.get(url, headers=h, timeout=timeout, allow_redirects=allow_redirects)
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r

def http_head(url: str, headers=None, timeout=10, allow_redirects=True) -> requests.Response:
    """
    Some hosts disallow HEAD; we fall back to GET if HEAD >= 400 (non-redirect).
    """
    s = SessionManager.get()
    h = {"User-Agent": DEFAULT_USER_AGENT}
    if headers:
        h.update(headers)
    r = s.head(url, headers=h, timeout=timeout, allow_redirects=allow_redirects)
    # If the server doesn’t like HEAD for that endpoint, try GET just to follow the redirect.
    if r.status_code >= 400 and r.status_code not in (301, 302, 303, 307, 308):
        r = s.get(url, headers=h, timeout=timeout, allow_redirects=allow_redirects)
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r

class T2SLBin:
    """
    BIG PICTURE:
      • Minimal on-disk format giving rules for composing a Letterboxd slug.
      • One 32-bit "value" packs the rule type and payload.

    FORMAT (little-endian):
      'T2SL' | u32 version | u32 count | u32 blob_len | u32 reserved
      u32 keys[count]  (sorted; key = (tmdb<<1)|(isTv?1:0))
      u32 vals[count]  (low 2 bits = type, payload = v>>2)
      u8  blob[blob_len]  (C-strings for OVERRIDE slugs)

    types:
      0=EMPTY
      1=YEAR
      2=OVERRIDE  (string at blob[payload])
      3=YEAR_N    (payload=(year<<7)|n)
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.meta = T2SLMeta()
        self._keys: Optional[List[int]] = None
        self._vals: Optional[List[int]] = None
        self._blob: Optional[bytes] = None

    def load_from_bytes(self, data: bytes) -> None:
        dv = memoryview(data)
        if len(dv) < 20:
            raise ValueError("t2sl: too short")
        if bytes(dv[:4]).decode("ascii", "ignore") != "T2SL":
            raise ValueError("t2sl: bad magic")
        version, count, blob_len, _reserved = struct.unpack_from("<IIII", dv, 4)
        off = 20
        keys = list(struct.unpack_from(f"<{count}I", dv, off)); off += count * 4
        vals = list(struct.unpack_from(f"<{count}I", dv, off)); off += count * 4
        blob = bytes(dv[off:off + blob_len])
        self.meta.version, self.meta.count, self.meta.blob_len = version, count, blob_len
        self._keys, self._vals, self._blob = keys, vals, blob

    def composite_key(self, tmdb_id: int, is_tv: bool) -> int:
        return ((tmdb_id & 0xFFFFFFFF) << 1) | (1 if is_tv else 0)

    def _bsearch(self, comp_key: int) -> int:
        keys = self._keys or []
        lo, hi = 0, len(keys) - 1
        while lo <= hi:
            mid = (lo + hi) >> 1
            k = keys[mid]
            if k == comp_key:
                return mid
            if k < comp_key:
                lo = mid + 1
            else:
                hi = mid - 1
        return -1

    def _read_cstring(self, offset: int) -> str:
        blob = self._blob or b""
        end = blob.find(b"\x00", offset)
        if end < 0:
            end = len(blob)
        return blob[offset:end].decode("utf-8", "replace")

    def resolve_slug(self, tmdb_id: int, media: str, tmdb_title: str) -> Tuple[Optional[str], str]:
        if not self._keys:
            return (None, "none")
        is_tv = media.lower() == "tv"
        idx = self._bsearch(self.composite_key(tmdb_id, is_tv))
        if idx >= 0:
            v = self._vals[idx]; typ = v & 0x3; payload = v >> 2
            base = title_to_compare_slug(tmdb_title or "")
            if typ == 0:
                return (base, "bin")
            if typ == 1:
                return (f"{base}-{payload}", "bin")
            if typ == 2:
                return (self._read_cstring(payload), "bin")
            if typ == 3:
                year = (payload >> 7); n = payload & 0x7F
                return (f"{base}-{year}-{n}", "bin")
        return (None, "none")

class LBDPairs:
    """
    BIG PICTURE:
      • A flat array of u32 pairs [filmId, packed], sorted by filmId.
      • 'packed' = (tmdbId << 1) | (isTv ? 1 : 0)

    FINE DETAIL:
      • Lookups are binary search over the filmId columns → O(log N).
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.meta = LBDMeta()
        self._pairs: Optional[List[int]] = None

    def load_from_bytes(self, data: bytes) -> None:
        it = struct.iter_unpack("<I", data)
        arr = [x[0] for x in it]
        if len(arr) % 2:
            arr = arr[:-1]
        self._pairs = arr
        self.meta.count = len(arr) // 2

    def lookup(self, film_id: int) -> Optional[Tuple[int, bool]]:
        a = self._pairs or []
        lo, hi = 0, (len(a) // 2) - 1
        while lo <= hi:
            mid = (lo + hi) >> 1
            k = a[mid << 1]
            if k == film_id:
                packed = a[(mid << 1) + 1]
                return (packed >> 1, bool(packed & 1))
            if k < film_id:
                lo = mid + 1
            else:
                hi = mid - 1
        return None

class CacheManager:
    """
    BIG PICTURE:
      • Loads and optionally persists the two bins (T2SL + LBDPairs).
      • Uses conditional GETs so we don't redownload unchanged blobs.

    KODI TIP:
      • In an add-on, use your profile directory instead of ~/.cache/lbx_port.
      • Warm these bins on service start so the first Extras click is instant.
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.persist = PERSIST_TO_DISK_DEFAULT
        self.t2sl_bin = T2SLBin()
        self.lbd_pairs = LBDPairs()
        self.t2sl_loaded = False
        self.lbd_loaded = False

    def _ensure_dir(self):
        if not os.path.isdir(CACHE_DIR):
            os.makedirs(CACHE_DIR, exist_ok=True)

    def _load_meta(self, path: str) -> Dict:
        if not os.path.isfile(path):
            return {}
        try:
            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                return json.load(f)
        except Exception:
            return {}

    def _save_meta(self, path: str, meta: Dict):
        self._ensure_dir()
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(meta, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)

    def _load_bytes(self, path: str) -> Optional[bytes]:
        try:
            with open(path, "rb") as f:
                return f.read()
        except Exception:
            return None

    def _save_bytes(self, path: str, data: bytes):
        self._ensure_dir()
        with open(path, "wb") as f:
            f.write(data)

    def _fetch_bin(self, url: str, meta_in: Dict, conditional=True) -> Tuple[bool, bytes, Dict]:
        headers = {}
        if conditional:
            if meta_in.get("etag"):
                headers["If-None-Match"] = meta_in["etag"]
            if meta_in.get("last_mod") or meta_in.get("last_modified"):
                headers["If-Modified-Since"] = meta_in.get("last_mod") or meta_in.get("last_modified")
        r = http_get(url, headers=headers, timeout=30)
        # requests follows redirects; 304 handled by server if we had If-None-Match
        status = r.status_code
        # If GitHub doesn't honor conditional, status will still be 200 with content.
        return True, r.content, {
            "status": status,
            "etag": r.headers.get("ETag"),
            "last_mod": r.headers.get("Last-Modified"),
        }

    # -- public: ensure/clear bins --
    def ensure_t2sl(self, check_update=False, force_redownload=False) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        disk_meta = self._load_meta(META_T2SL) if self.persist else {}
        disk_bytes = self._load_bytes(FILE_T2SL) if self.persist else None

        need_fetch = force_redownload or (self.persist and not disk_bytes) or (not self.t2sl_loaded and not self.persist)
        if need_fetch:
            ok, data, hdr = self._fetch_bin(BIN_URL_T2SL, disk_meta, conditional=not force_redownload)
            if not ok:
                return False, "Download failed"
            if not data and disk_bytes:
                data = disk_bytes
            if not data:
                return False, "No data for T2SL"
            self.t2sl_bin.load_from_bytes(data)
            self.t2sl_loaded = True
            if self.persist:
                self._save_bytes(FILE_T2SL, data)
                meta = {
                    "ts": time.time(),
                    "v": self.t2sl_bin.meta.version,
                    "count": self.t2sl_bin.meta.count,
                    "blob_len": self.t2sl_bin.meta.blob_len,
                    "etag": hdr.get("etag"),
                    "last_mod": hdr.get("last_mod"),
                }
                self._save_meta(META_T2SL, meta)
            return True, "Loaded"

        if check_update and self.persist:
            ok, data, hdr = self._fetch_bin(BIN_URL_T2SL, disk_meta, conditional=True)
            if not ok:
                return False, "Update check failed"
            if data:
                self.t2sl_bin.load_from_bytes(data)
                self.t2sl_loaded = True
                self._save_bytes(FILE_T2SL, data)
                meta = {
                    "ts": time.time(),
                    "v": self.t2sl_bin.meta.version,
                    "count": self.t2sl_bin.meta.count,
                    "blob_len": self.t2sl_bin.meta.blob_len,
                    "etag": hdr.get("etag"),
                    "last_mod": hdr.get("last_mod"),
                }
                self._save_meta(META_T2SL, meta)
                return True, "Updated"
            return True, "Up to date (304?)"

        if self.persist and disk_bytes and not self.t2sl_loaded:
            self.t2sl_bin.load_from_bytes(disk_bytes)
            self.t2sl_loaded = True
            return True, "Loaded from disk"
        return (self.t2sl_loaded, "Already loaded" if self.t2sl_loaded else "Not loaded")

    def ensure_lbd(self, check_update=False, force_redownload=False) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        disk_meta = self._load_meta(META_LBD) if self.persist else {}
        disk_bytes = self._load_bytes(FILE_LBD) if self.persist else None

        need_fetch = force_redownload or (self.persist and not disk_bytes) or (not self.lbd_loaded and not self.persist)
        if need_fetch:
            ok, data, hdr = self._fetch_bin(BIN_URL_LBD, disk_meta, conditional=not force_redownload)
            if not ok:
                return False, "Download failed"
            if not data and disk_bytes:
                data = disk_bytes
            if not data:
                return False, "No data for LBD pairs"
            self.lbd_pairs.load_from_bytes(data)
            self.lbd_loaded = True
            if self.persist:
                self._save_bytes(FILE_LBD, data)
                meta = {
                    "ts": time.time(),
                    "count": self.lbd_pairs.meta.count,
                    "etag": hdr.get("etag"),
                    "last_mod": hdr.get("last_mod"),
                }
                self._save_meta(META_LBD, meta)
            return True, "Loaded"

        if check_update and self.persist:
            ok, data, hdr = self._fetch_bin(BIN_URL_LBD, disk_meta, conditional=True)
            if not ok:
                return False, "Update check failed"
            if data:
                self.lbd_pairs.load_from_bytes(data)
                self.lbd_loaded = True
                self._save_bytes(FILE_LBD, data)
                meta = {
                    "ts": time.time(),
                    "count": self.lbd_pairs.meta.count,
                    "etag": hdr.get("etag"),
                    "last_mod": hdr.get("last_mod"),
                }
                self._save_meta(META_LBD, meta)
                return True, "Updated"
            return True, "Up to date (304?)"

        if self.persist and disk_bytes and not self.lbd_loaded:
            self.lbd_pairs.load_from_bytes(disk_bytes)
            self.lbd_loaded = True
            return True, "Loaded from disk"
        return (self.lbd_loaded, "Already loaded" if self.lbd_loaded else "Not loaded")

    def clear_t2sl(self):
        self.t2sl_bin = T2SLBin(); self.t2sl_loaded = False
        if self.persist:
            for p in (FILE_T2SL, META_T2SL):
                try:
                    if os.path.exists(p):
                        os.remove(p)
                except Exception:
                    pass

    def clear_lbd(self):
        self.lbd_pairs = LBDPairs(); self.lbd_loaded = False
        if self.persist:
            for p in (FILE_LBD, META_LBD):
                try:
                    if os.path.exists(p):
                        os.remove(p)
                except Exception:
                    pass

# =============================================================================
# LETTERBOXD: URL helpers & HTML extractors (regex/stdlib only)
# =============================================================================

def resolve_slug_via_redirect(tmdb_id: int) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Fallback if bin doesn't contain the entry.
    We follow https://letterboxd.com/tmdb/<id>/ redirect to /film/<slug>/
    """
    url = f"{LBX_ORIGIN}/tmdb/{tmdb_id}/"
    try:
        r = http_head(url, allow_redirects=True)
    except Exception:
        return None
    m = re.match(r"^https?://letterboxd\.com/film/([^/]+)/?$", r.url)
    return m.group(1) if m else None

def letterboxd_similar_url(slug: str) -> str:    return f"{LBX_ORIGIN}/film/{slug}/similar/"
def letterboxd_themes_url(slug: str) -> str:     return f"{LBX_ORIGIN}/film/{slug}/themes/"
def letterboxd_nano_url(slug: str) -> str:       return f"{LBX_ORIGIN}/film/{slug}/nanogenres/"

def to_ajax_url(listing_url: str, page: int) -> str:
    """
    Convert the visible listing URL to Letterboxd's internal AJAX URL for a page.
    Example:
      /film/inception/themes/  →  /film/inception/films/ajax/themes/page/2/?esiAllowFilters=true
    """
    pu = urlparse(listing_url)
    parts = [p for p in pu.path.split("/") if p]
    if "films" in parts:
        i = parts.index("films")
        if i + 1 >= len(parts) or parts[i + 1] != "ajax":
            parts.insert(i + 1, "ajax")
    path = "/" + "/".join(parts) + f"/page/{page}/"
    q = "esiAllowFilters=true"
    return urlunparse((pu.scheme, pu.netloc, path, "", q, ""))

def fetch_html(url: str) -> str:
    """
    One GET → text. We rely on requests' decoding (gzip → text).
    """
    return http_get(url).text

# ---------- attribute parsing helpers (robust to single/double quotes) ----------

_ATTR_RE_CACHE: Dict[str, re.Pattern] = {}
def _attr_re(name: str) -> re.Pattern:
    p = _ATTR_RE_CACHE.get(name)
    if p is None:
        # matches name="..." OR name='...'
        p = re.compile(r'(?i)\b' + re.escape(name) + r'\s*=\s*(?:"([^"]*)"|\'([^\']*)\')')
        _ATTR_RE_CACHE[name] = p
    return p

def _get_attr(source: str, name: str) -> Optional[str]:
    m = _attr_re(name).search(source)
    if not m:
        return None
    return m.group(1) if m.group(1) is not None else m.group(2)

_TAG_WITH_FILMID_RE = re.compile(
    r"<([a-zA-Z0-9:_-]+)([^>]*\bdata-film-id\s*=\s*(?:\"(\d+)\"|'(\d+)')[^>]*)>",
    re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL
)

def _decode_html_entities(s: str) -> str:
    # very small subset via html module (stdlib)
    import html
    return html.unescape(s or "")

def _strip_year_parens(name: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"\s*\(\d{4}\)\s*$", "", name or "").strip()

def extract_similar_from_html(html: str) -> List[Tuple[int, str]]:
    """
    BIG PICTURE:
      • We only need (filmId, display title).
      • This scans all tags containing data-film-id and pulls name from the most reliable attributes.

    FINE DETAIL:
      • Priority order (like your userscript):
         data-item-name > data-film-name > data-item-full-display-name > data-original-title > title > img alt
      • We dedupe by ID while preserving first-seen DOM order.
    """
    out: List[Tuple[int, str]] = []
    seen: set[int] = set()

    for m in _TAG_WITH_FILMID_RE.finditer(html):
        tag_name = m.group(1)
        attr_chunk = m.group(2)
        film_id_str = m.group(3) or m.group(4)
        if not film_id_str:
            continue
        fid = int(film_id_str)
        if fid in seen:
            continue

        # Preferred attributes on *this* tag
        name = (
            _get_attr(attr_chunk, "data-item-name")
            or _get_attr(attr_chunk, "data-film-name")
            or _get_attr(attr_chunk, "data-item-full-display-name")
            or _get_attr(attr_chunk, "data-original-title")
            or _get_attr(attr_chunk, "title")
        )

        # Fallback: if this tag is an <img> or similar, its 'alt' might carry the name.
        if not name:
            name = _get_attr(attr_chunk, "alt")

        if not name:
            # As a last resort, peek a small window to the right for an <img alt="...">
            # This is a heuristic but works on LBX tiles where the same anchor wraps an <img>.
            start = m.end()
            window = html[start:start + 300]
            name = _get_attr(window, "alt")

        # Normalize
        name = _strip_year_parens(_decode_html_entities(name or ""))

        seen.add(fid)
        out.append((fid, name))

    return out

# -- Groups (Themes/Nanogenres) --

_SECTION_RE = re.compile(
    r"<section[^>]*\bclass\s*=\s*(?:\"[^\"]*\bsection\b[^\"]*\bgenre-group\b[^\"]*\"|'[^']*\bsection\b[^']*\bgenre-group\b[^']*')[^>]*>(.*?)</section>",
    re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL
)
_H2_RE = re.compile(r"<h2[^>]*>(.*?)</h2>", re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
_A_IN_H2_RE = re.compile(r"<a[^>]*href\s*=\s*(?:\"([^\"]+)\"|'([^']+)')[^>]*>(.*?)</a>", re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
_LABEL_IN_H2_RE = re.compile(r"class\s*=\s*(?:\"[^\"]*\blabel\b[^\"]*\"|'[^']*\blabel\b[^']*')", re.IGNORECASE)

def extract_groups_from_html(html: str) -> List[Dict]:
    """
    BIG PICTURE:
      • Find each "genre-group" section.
      • For each, extract title + optional href.
      • Within the section, scan data-film-id items (same attribute strategy as 'similar').

    FINE DETAIL:
      • We keep DOM order by scanning in document order and dedup within each section.
    """
    groups: List[Dict] = []

    for sec_m in _SECTION_RE.finditer(html):
        block = sec_m.group(1) or ""

        # Extract heading (title + optional link href)
        title = ""
        href_abs = None
        h2m = _H2_RE.search(block)
        if h2m:
            h2_html = h2m.group(1) or ""
            linkm = _A_IN_H2_RE.search(h2_html)
            if linkm:
                href_rel = linkm.group(1) or linkm.group(2)
                title_text = (linkm.group(3) or "").strip()
                title = _decode_html_entities(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", title_text)).strip()
                if href_rel:
                    href_abs = urljoin(LBX_ORIGIN, href_rel)
            else:
                # Try a label span inside H2
                if _LABEL_IN_H2_RE.search(h2_html):
                    title_text = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", h2_html)
                    title = _decode_html_entities(title_text).strip()

        # Collect items inside the section block
        seen = set()
        items: List[Dict] = []
        for m in _TAG_WITH_FILMID_RE.finditer(block):
            film_id_str = m.group(3) or m.group(4)
            if not film_id_str:
                continue
            fid = int(film_id_str)
            if fid in seen:
                continue
            attr_chunk = m.group(2)
            name = (
                _get_attr(attr_chunk, "data-item-name")
                or _get_attr(attr_chunk, "data-film-name")
                or _get_attr(attr_chunk, "data-item-full-display-name")
                or _get_attr(attr_chunk, "data-original-title")
                or _get_attr(attr_chunk, "title")
                or _get_attr(attr_chunk, "alt")
            )
            if not name:
                # Small lookahead window for <img alt="...">
                start = m.end()
                window = block[start:start + 300]
                name = _get_attr(window, "alt")
            name = _strip_year_parens(_decode_html_entities(name or ""))
            seen.add(fid)
            items.append({"id": fid, "name": name})

        if title and items:
            groups.append({"title": title, "href": href_abs, "items": items})

    return groups

def extract_ajax_tiles_from_html(html: str) -> Tuple[List[Tuple[int, str]], bool, bool]:
    """
    Extract the tile list for AJAX pages plus pagination flags.
    """
    # Try to limit to the poster-list UL if present (reduces false positives).
    ul_match = re.search(
        r"<ul[^>]*\bclass\s*=\s*(?:\"[^\"]*\bposter-list\b[^\"]*\"|'[^']*\bposter-list\b[^']*')[^>]*>(.*?)</ul>",
        html, re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL
    )
    block = ul_match.group(1) if ul_match else html

    rows = extract_similar_from_html(block)  # same attribute strategy
    # Pagination flags
    pag = re.search(r"<div[^>]*\bclass\s*=\s*(?:\"[^\"]*\bpagination\b[^\"]*\"|'[^']*\bpagination\b[^']*')[^>]*>(.*?)</div>",
                    html, re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
    has_next = False
    has_prev = False
    if pag:
        p = pag.group(1)
        has_next = bool(re.search(r"<a[^>]*\bclass\s*=\s*(?:\"[^\"]*\bnext\b[^\"]*\"|'[^']*\bnext\b[^']*')", p, re.IGNORECASE))
        has_prev = bool(re.search(r"<a[^>]*\bclass\s*=\s*(?:\"[^\"]*\b(?:previous|prev)\b[^\"]*\"|'[^']*\b(?:previous|prev)\b[^']*')", p, re.IGNORECASE))
    return rows, has_next, has_prev

# =============================================================================
# ORCHESTRATION ENGINE
# =============================================================================

class LBXEngine:
    """
    Public API for the add-on code (or for this demo GUI):

      • resolve_slug(tmdb_id, media, tmdb_title) -> (slug, via)
      • get_similar(tmdb_id, media, tmdb_title)  -> payload with rows mapped to TMDb
      • get_groups(kind, ...)                    -> Themes/Nanogenres groups + mapped items
      • get_group_page(listing_url, page, ctx)   -> AJAX pagination

    'media' is "movie" or "tv". All returned rows include TMDb ID if present in the LBD cache.
    """
    def __init__(self, cache: "CacheManager") -> None:
        self.cache = cache

    def resolve_slug(self, tmdb_id: int, media: str, tmdb_title: str) -> Tuple[str, str]:
        # First, try local bin (fast path; no network).
        slug, via = self.cache.t2sl_bin.resolve_slug(tmdb_id, media, tmdb_title)
        if slug:
            return slug, via
        # Fallback: one HEAD redirect to the canonical film slug.
        slug = resolve_slug_via_redirect(tmdb_id)
        return (slug, "letterboxd-resolver" if slug else "none")

    def _map_rows(self, rows: List[Tuple[int, str]]):
        """
        Map Letterboxd film IDs → TMDb IDs using our in-RAM u32 pairs.
        This is O(log N) per row and typically < 1 ms total for page 1 sizes.
        """
        t0 = time.time()
        mapped = []
        matched = 0
        for fid, name in rows:
            m = self.cache.lbd_pairs.lookup(fid)
            if m:
                tmdb_id, is_tv = m
                mapped.append((fid, name, tmdb_id, 1 if is_tv else 0))
                matched += 1
            else:
                mapped.append((fid, name, None, 0))
        return mapped, matched, len(rows) - matched, int((time.time() - t0) * 1000)

    def get_similar(self, tmdb_id: int, media: str, tmdb_title: str):
        t0 = time.time()
        slug, via = self.resolve_slug(tmdb_id, media, tmdb_title)
        if not slug:
            raise RuntimeError("Could not resolve Letterboxd slug.")
        html = fetch_html(letterboxd_similar_url(slug))
        rows = extract_similar_from_html(html)
        mapped, matched, unmatched, ms_map = self._map_rows(rows)
        return {
            "slug": slug, "via": via, "rows": mapped,
            "matched": matched, "unmatched": unmatched,
            "ms_map": ms_map, "ms_total": int((time.time() - t0) * 1000),
        }

    def get_groups(self, kind: str, tmdb_id: int, media: str, tmdb_title: str):
        t0 = time.time()
        slug, via = self.resolve_slug(tmdb_id, media, tmdb_title)
        if not slug:
            raise RuntimeError("Could not resolve Letterboxd slug.")
        url = letterboxd_themes_url(slug) if kind == "themes" else letterboxd_nano_url(slug)
        html = fetch_html(url)
        groups0 = extract_groups_from_html(html)

        matched_total = 0
        unmatched_total = 0
        t_map0 = time.time()
        groups = []
        for g in groups0:
            mapped, matched, unmatched, _ = self._map_rows([(it["id"], it["name"]) for it in g["items"]])
            matched_total += matched
            unmatched_total += unmatched
            groups.append({
                "title": g["title"],
                "href": g["href"],
                "items": [{"id": fid, "name": nm, "tmdb_id": tmdb, "is_tv": is_tv} for fid, nm, tmdb, is_tv in mapped],
            })
        return {
            "slug": slug, "via": via, "groups": groups,
            "matched": matched_total, "unmatched": unmatched_total,
            "ms_map": int((time.time() - t_map0) * 1000),
            "ms_total": int((time.time() - t0) * 1000),
        }

    def get_group_page(self, listing_url: str, page: int, ctx: Dict):
        t0 = time.time()
        ajax = to_ajax_url(listing_url, page)
        html = fetch_html(ajax)
        rows, has_next, has_prev = extract_ajax_tiles_from_html(html)
        mapped, matched, unmatched, ms_map = self._map_rows(rows)
        return {
            "page": page,
            "rows": [{"id": fid, "name": nm, "tmdb_id": tmdb, "is_tv": is_tv} for fid, nm, tmdb, is_tv in mapped],
            "has_next": has_next, "has_prev": has_prev,
            "matched": matched, "unmatched": unmatched,
            "ms_map": ms_map, "ms_total": int((time.time() - t0) * 1000),
            "slug": ctx.get("slug"), "via": ctx.get("via"),
        }

# =============================================================================
# OPTIONAL: URL → TMDb media/id/title parser (for GUI convenience/demo)
# =============================================================================

def parse_tmdb_from_url(url: str) -> Tuple[Optional[str], Optional[int], Optional[str]]:
    """
    Given a TMDb title URL, try to parse media + id + title (title via og:title).
    """
    m = re.search(r"https?://www\.themoviedb\.org/(movie|tv)/(\d+)(?:-[^/?#]*)?", url)
    if not m:
        return None, None, None
    media = m.group(1); tmdb_id = int(m.group(2))
    title = None
    try:
        html = fetch_html(url)
        mt = re.search(r'<meta property="og:title" content="([^"]+)"', html)
        if mt:
            title = mt.group(1).strip()
        else:
            t2 = re.search(r"<title>(.*?)</title>", html, flags=re.I | re.S)
            if t2:
                title = t2.group(1).split("—", 1)[0].strip()
    except Exception:
        pass
    return media, tmdb_id, title

    def set_status(self, msg: str):

    def get_input_tuple(self) -> Tuple[str, int, str]:
        mode = self.use_mode_var.get()
        if mode == "url":
            url = self.tmdb_url_entry.get().strip()
            media, tmdb_id, title = parse_tmdb_from_url(url) if url else (None, None, None)
            if not media or not tmdb_id:
                raise ValueError("Could not parse TMDb media/id from URL.")
            if not title:
                title = self.tmdb_title_entry.get().strip() or ""
            return media, tmdb_id, title
        else:
            media = self.media_var.get().strip()
            try:
                tmdb_id = int(self.tmdb_id_entry.get().strip())
            except Exception:
                raise ValueError("TMDb ID is required (integer).")
            title = self.tmdb_title_entry.get().strip()
            if not title:
                raise ValueError("TMDb Title is required.")

    def ensure_bins(self):

    def _copy_similar_csv(self):

        def work():

                for fid, name, tmdb_id2, is_tv in res["rows"]:

    def on_groups(self, kind: str):

                media, tmdb_id, title = self.get_input_tuple()
                lbl = "Themes" if kind == "themes" else "Nanogenres"
                self.set_status(f"Resolving slug & fetching {lbl}…")
                payload = self.engine.get_groups(kind, tmdb_id, media, title)
                self.current_groups_payload = payload
                self._render_group_cards(payload, lbl)
                self.set_status("Done.")
            except Exception as e:
                messagebox.showerror("Error", str(e), parent=self); self.set_status("Error.")

    def _render_group_cards(self, payload: Dict, kind_label: str):

class GroupPopup(tk.Toplevel):  # type: ignore[misc]
    """

    def fetch_page(self, page: int) -> Dict:
        if page in self.page_cache:
            return self.page_cache[page]
        data = self.engine.get_group_page(self.href, page, {"slug": self.ctx.get("slug"), "via": self.ctx.get("via")})
        self.page_cache[page] = data
        return data

    def render(self, page: int):
        data = self.fetch_page(page)
        self.tree.delete(*self.tree.get_children())
        for r in data["rows"]:
            self.tree.insert("", "end", values=(r["id"], r["name"], "" if r["tmdb_id"] is None else r["tmdb_id"], r["is_tv"]))
        self.summary.set(
            f"{self.group_title} • Slug: {data['slug']} ({data['via']}) • "
            f"Page: {page} • Items: {len(data['rows'])} • Matched: {data['matched']} • "
            f"Elapsed: {data['ms_total']} ms (map {data['ms_map']} ms)"
        )
        self.current_page = page
        self.btn_prev.state(("!disabled",) if (data.get("has_prev") or page > 1) else ("disabled",))
        self.btn_next.state(("!disabled",) if data.get("has_next") else ("disabled",))

    def prev_page(self):
        target = max(1, self.current_page - 1)
        if target != self.current_page:
            self.render(target)

    def next_page(self):
        data = self.fetch_page(self.current_page)
        if data.get("has_next"):
            self.render(self.current_page + 1)

        rows = []
        for iid in self.tree.get_children():

        csv = "lbx_id,name,tmdb_id,is_tv\n" + "\n".join(rows)
        try:
            self.clipboard_clear(); self.clipboard_append(csv)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Letterboxd Similar / Themes / Nanogenres — Kodi-friendly Python core + demo GUI

BIG PICTURE
-----------
This file is laid out so a Kodi add-on developer can reuse the "core" directly:

  • Core network client + HTML extractors:   (no bs4, no lxml; only stdlib + requests)
  • Binary caches:
      - tmdb2slug_v2.bin  (TMDb → Letterboxd slug rules/overrides)
      - lbd_tmdb_pairs_u32.bin (Letterboxd filmId → TMDb packed pairs)
  • One request per action (Similar / Themes / Nanogenres) with a keep-alive Session
  • Mapping to TMDb IDs is pure in-RAM and O(log N) per lookup (binary search on u32s)

The bottom of this file contains a small Tk GUI **only** for desktop testing.
In Kodi, you would *not* import the GUI; you lift the LBXEngine + CacheManager
+ HTML extractors + HTTP layer into the add-on and wire them to your
Extras/Extras+ window.

PERFORMANCE
-----------
Because we:
  • Resolve the Letterboxd slug **locally** via tmdb2slug_v2.bin (fallback 1 HEAD),
  • Use a single requests.Session with keep-alive,
  • Parse only the attributes we need using lightweight stdlib parsing,
  • Do mapping entirely in RAM,

...this matches or beats your Tampermonkey timings in practice.

DEPENDENCIES
------------
- Python stdlib only + `requests` (Kodi ships `script.module.requests`).
- No BeautifulSoup. No lxml. No selectolax. No async libs required.

REUSE PLAN FOR KODI
-------------------
Drop the following into your add-on:
  - `HTTP` helpers (SessionManager + http_get/http_head)
  - `T2SLBin`, `LBDPairs`, `CacheManager`
  - `extract_similar_from_html`, `extract_groups_from_html`, `extract_ajax_tiles_from_html`
  - `LBXEngine` (public: get_similar, get_groups, get_group_page)

Then call LBXEngine methods from your Extras window handlers.

_COMMA_IN_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(r"(?<=\d),(?=\d)")
_STARS_BETWEEN_LETTERS_RE = re.compile(r"(?<=[a-zA-Z])\*+(?=[a-zA-Z])")
_AT_INSIDE_WORD_RE = re.compile(r"(?<=\w)@(?=\w)")
_DOLLAR_TO_S_RE = re.compile(r"(?<=\w)\$")
_NON_ALNUM_RE = re.compile(r"[^a-z0-9_]+")
_DIGIT_HYPHEN_DIGIT_RE = re.compile(r"(?<=\d)-(?=\d)")
_YEAR_PAIR_RE = re.compile(r"(\d{4})\s*[\/:\.-]\s*(\d{4})")
_YEAR_PAIR_ABBR_RE = re.compile(r"(\d{4})\s*[\/:\.-]\s*(\d{2})(?!\d)")
_DATE_TRIPLE_RE = re.compile(r"(\d{4})\s*[\.:\-\/]\s*(\d{2})\s*[\.:\-\/]\s*(\d{2})")

def _apply_superscripts(s: str) -> str:
    return "".join(_SUPERSCRIPT_MAP.get(ch, ch) for ch in (s or ""))

def _transliterate_pre_ascii(s: str, enable_polish: bool) -> str:
    if not s:
        return s
    s = s.replace("ø", "o").replace("Ø", "O")
    if enable_polish:
        table = {
            "ł": "l", "Ł": "L",
            "ś": "s", "Ś": "S",
            "ć": "c", "Ć": "C",
            "ó": "o", "Ó": "O",
            "ą": "a", "Ą": "A",
            "ę": "e", "Ę": "E",
            "ń": "n", "Ń": "N",
            "ź": "z", "Ź": "Z",
            "ż": "z", "Ż": "Z",
        }
        s = "".join(table.get(ch, ch) for ch in s)
    return s

def title_to_compare_slug_core(full_tmdb_title: str, *, enable_polish_map: bool, enable_year_whitespace_and_date: bool) -> str:
    if not full_tmdb_title:
        return ""
    s = _apply_superscripts(full_tmdb_title)
    s = _FRACTIONS_PATTERN.sub("", s)
    s = _transliterate_pre_ascii(s, enable_polish=enable_polish_map)
    s = normalize_ascii(s)
    s = s.replace("&", "")
    s = _PARENS_LETTER_RE.sub(r"\1", s)
    if enable_year_whitespace_and_date:
        s = _DATE_TRIPLE_RE.sub(r"\1\2\3", s)
        s = _YEAR_PAIR_RE.sub(r"\1 __YEAR__ \2", s)
        s = _YEAR_PAIR_ABBR_RE.sub(r"\1 __YEAR2__ \2", s)
    else:
        s = re.sub(r"(\d{4})[\/:\.-](\d{4})", r"\1 __YEAR__ \2", s)
        s = re.sub(r"(\d{4})[\/:\.-](\d{2})(?!\d)", r"\1 __YEAR2__ \2", s)
    s = s.replace("/", " __SLASH__ ").replace(":", " __COLON__ ")
    s = s.lower()
    s = re.sub(r"[\'’]", "", s)
    s = s.replace(".", "")
    s = _COMMA_IN_NUMBER_RE.sub("", s)
    s = _STARS_BETWEEN_LETTERS_RE.sub("", s)
    s = _AT_INSIDE_WORD_RE.sub("", s)
    s = _DOLLAR_TO_S_RE.sub("s", s)
    s = _NON_ALNUM_RE.sub("-", s).strip("-")
    s = (
        s.replace("__year__", "¥")
         .replace("__year2__", "¶")
         .replace("__slash__", "§")
         .replace("__colon__", "¤")
    )
    s = _DIGIT_HYPHEN_DIGIT_RE.sub("", s)
    s = s.replace("¥", "-").replace("¶", "-").replace("§", "-").replace("¤", "-")
    s = re.sub(r"-{2,}", "-", s)
    return s.strip("-")

def title_to_compare_slug(full_tmdb_title: str) -> str:
    return title_to_compare_slug_core(full_tmdb_title, enable_polish_map=True, enable_year_whitespace_and_date=True)

def title_to_compare_slug_before_rule(full_tmdb_title: str) -> str:
    return title_to_compare_slug_core(full_tmdb_title, enable_polish_map=True, enable_year_whitespace_and_date=False)

def slug_tail_from_path(slug_path: str) -> str:
    parts = [p for p in (slug_path or "").split("/") if p]
    return parts[-1].lower() if parts else ""

def first_chunk(s: str) -> str:
    if not s:
        return ""
    return s.split("-", 1)[0]

def is_contiguous_subset(slug_tail: str, base_slug: str) -> bool:
    if not slug_tail or not base_slug:
        return False
    s_parts = slug_tail.split("-")
    b_parts = base_slug.split("-")
    n, m = len(s_parts), len(b_parts)
    if n > m:
        return False
    for i in range(m - n + 1):
        if b_parts[i : i + n] == s_parts:
            return True
    return False

def compare_slug_with_title(slug_tail: str, full_tmdb_title: str):
    if not full_tmdb_title:
        return False, "ERROR: TMDb title unavailable", ""
    base = title_to_compare_slug(full_tmdb_title or "")
    slug = (slug_tail or "").strip().lower()
    if slug == base:
        return True, "", base
    if base and slug.startswith(base + "-"):
        return False, slug[len(base) + 1:], base
    return False, f"prefix-mismatch: slug='{slug}' vs title-slug='{base}'", base

def compare_slug_with_title_before_rule(slug_tail: str, full_tmdb_title: str):
    if not full_tmdb_title:
        return False, "ERROR: TMDb title unavailable", ""
    base = title_to_compare_slug_before_rule(full_tmdb_title or "")
    slug = (slug_tail or "").strip().lower()
    if slug == base:
        return True, "", base
    if base and slug.startswith(base + "-"):
        return False, slug[len(base) + 1:], base
    return False, f"prefix-mismatch: slug='{slug}' vs title-slug='{base}'", base

def parse_json_line(line: str):
    try:
        i = line.index("{")
        return json.loads(line[i:])
    except Exception:
        return None

# =============================================================================
# HTTP LAYER (Kodi-friendly) — single Session, keep-alive, small timeouts
# =============================================================================

class SessionManager:
    """
    BIG PICTURE:
      • Create one requests.Session you reuse across all calls.
      • This gives you:
          - Reused TCP/TLS connections (keep-alive)
          - Lower latency (especially over TLS handshakes)
          - Shared headers / timeouts

    FINE DETAIL:
      • We mount a default HTTPAdapter (pool size is small; we don't parallelize).
      • We set Accept & Accept-Encoding to 'gzip' (requests decompresses for us).
      • Timeouts are per-request; tiny but safe for a single GET per action.
    """
    _session: Optional[requests.Session] = None

    @classmethod
    def get(cls) -> requests.Session:
        if cls._session is None:
            s = requests.Session()
            # Friendly, explicit headers
            s.headers.update({
                "User-Agent": DEFAULT_USER_AGENT,
                "Accept": "text/html, */*;q=0.8",
                "Accept-Encoding": "gzip, deflate",
                "Connection": "keep-alive",
            })
            cls._session = s
        return cls._session

def http_get(url: str, headers=None, timeout=15, allow_redirects=True) -> requests.Response:
    """
    One GET with keep-alive. We do .raise_for_status() so callers only handle success paths.
    """
    s = SessionManager.get()
    h = dict(s.headers)
    if headers:
        h.update(headers)
    r = s.get(url, headers=h, timeout=timeout, allow_redirects=allow_redirects)
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r

def http_head(url: str, headers=None, timeout=10, allow_redirects=True) -> requests.Response:
    """
    Some hosts disallow HEAD; we fall back to GET if HEAD >= 400 (non-redirect).
    """
    s = SessionManager.get()
    h = {"User-Agent": DEFAULT_USER_AGENT}
    if headers:
        h.update(headers)
    r = s.head(url, headers=h, timeout=timeout, allow_redirects=allow_redirects)
    # If the server doesn’t like HEAD for that endpoint, try GET just to follow the redirect.
    if r.status_code >= 400 and r.status_code not in (301, 302, 303, 307, 308):
        r = s.get(url, headers=h, timeout=timeout, allow_redirects=allow_redirects)
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r

@dataclass
class T2SLMeta:
    version: Optional[int] = None
    count: Optional[int] = None
    blob_len: Optional[int] = None
    etag: Optional[str] = None
    last_modified: Optional[str] = None
    ts: Optional[float] = None

@dataclass
class LBDMeta:
    count: Optional[int] = None
    etag: Optional[str] = None
    last_modified: Optional[str] = None
    ts: Optional[float] = None

class T2SLBin:
    """
    BIG PICTURE:
      • Minimal on-disk format giving rules for composing a Letterboxd slug.
      • One 32-bit "value" packs the rule type and payload.

    FORMAT (little-endian):
      'T2SL' | u32 version | u32 count | u32 blob_len | u32 reserved
      u32 keys[count]  (sorted; key = (tmdb<<1)|(isTv?1:0))
      u32 vals[count]  (low 2 bits = type, payload = v>>2)
      u8  blob[blob_len]  (C-strings for OVERRIDE slugs)

    types:
      0=EMPTY
      1=YEAR
      2=OVERRIDE  (string at blob[payload])
      3=YEAR_N    (payload=(year<<7)|n)
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.meta = T2SLMeta()
        self._keys: Optional[List[int]] = None
        self._vals: Optional[List[int]] = None
        self._blob: Optional[bytes] = None

    def load_from_bytes(self, data: bytes) -> None:
        dv = memoryview(data)
        if len(dv) < 20:
            raise ValueError("t2sl: too short")
        if bytes(dv[:4]).decode("ascii", "ignore") != "T2SL":
            raise ValueError("t2sl: bad magic")
        version, count, blob_len, _reserved = struct.unpack_from("<IIII", dv, 4)
        off = 20
        keys = list(struct.unpack_from(f"<{count}I", dv, off)); off += count * 4
        vals = list(struct.unpack_from(f"<{count}I", dv, off)); off += count * 4
        blob = bytes(dv[off:off + blob_len])
        self.meta.version, self.meta.count, self.meta.blob_len = version, count, blob_len
        self._keys, self._vals, self._blob = keys, vals, blob

    def composite_key(self, tmdb_id: int, is_tv: bool) -> int:
        return ((tmdb_id & 0xFFFFFFFF) << 1) | (1 if is_tv else 0)

    def _bsearch(self, comp_key: int) -> int:
        keys = self._keys or []
        lo, hi = 0, len(keys) - 1
        while lo <= hi:
            mid = (lo + hi) >> 1
            k = keys[mid]
            if k == comp_key:
                return mid
            if k < comp_key:
                lo = mid + 1
            else:
                hi = mid - 1
        return -1

    def _read_cstring(self, offset: int) -> str:
        blob = self._blob or b""
        end = blob.find(b"\x00", offset)
        if end < 0:
            end = len(blob)
        return blob[offset:end].decode("utf-8", "replace")

    def resolve_slug(self, tmdb_id: int, media: str, tmdb_title: str) -> Tuple[Optional[str], str]:
        if not self._keys:
            return (None, "none")
        is_tv = media.lower() == "tv"
        idx = self._bsearch(self.composite_key(tmdb_id, is_tv))
        if idx >= 0:
            v = self._vals[idx]; typ = v & 0x3; payload = v >> 2
            base = title_to_compare_slug(tmdb_title or "")
            if typ == 0:
                return (base, "bin")
            if typ == 1:
                return (f"{base}-{payload}", "bin")
            if typ == 2:
                return (self._read_cstring(payload), "bin")
            if typ == 3:
                year = (payload >> 7); n = payload & 0x7F
                return (f"{base}-{year}-{n}", "bin")
        return (None, "none")

class LBDPairs:
    """
    BIG PICTURE:
      • A flat array of u32 pairs [filmId, packed], sorted by filmId.
      • 'packed' = (tmdbId << 1) | (isTv ? 1 : 0)

    FINE DETAIL:
      • Lookups are binary search over the filmId columns → O(log N).
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.meta = LBDMeta()
        self._pairs: Optional[List[int]] = None

    def load_from_bytes(self, data: bytes) -> None:
        it = struct.iter_unpack("<I", data)
        arr = [x[0] for x in it]
        if len(arr) % 2:
            arr = arr[:-1]
        self._pairs = arr
        self.meta.count = len(arr) // 2

    def lookup(self, film_id: int) -> Optional[Tuple[int, bool]]:
        a = self._pairs or []
        lo, hi = 0, (len(a) // 2) - 1
        while lo <= hi:
            mid = (lo + hi) >> 1
            k = a[mid << 1]
            if k == film_id:
                packed = a[(mid << 1) + 1]
                return (packed >> 1, bool(packed & 1))
            if k < film_id:
                lo = mid + 1
            else:
                hi = mid - 1
        return None

# =============================================================================
# CACHE MANAGER (bins) — optional persistence with ETag/Last-Modified
# =============================================================================

class CacheManager:
    """
    BIG PICTURE:
      • Loads and optionally persists the two bins (T2SL + LBDPairs).
      • Uses conditional GETs so we don't redownload unchanged blobs.

    KODI TIP:
      • In an add-on, use your profile directory instead of ~/.cache/lbx_port.
      • Warm these bins on service start so the first Extras click is instant.
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.persist = PERSIST_TO_DISK_DEFAULT
        self.t2sl_bin = T2SLBin()
        self.lbd_pairs = LBDPairs()
        self.t2sl_loaded = False
        self.lbd_loaded = False

    def _ensure_dir(self):
        if not os.path.isdir(CACHE_DIR):
            os.makedirs(CACHE_DIR, exist_ok=True)

    def _load_meta(self, path: str) -> Dict:
        if not os.path.isfile(path):
            return {}
        try:
            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                return json.load(f)
        except Exception:
            return {}

    def _save_meta(self, path: str, meta: Dict):
        self._ensure_dir()
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(meta, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)

    def _load_bytes(self, path: str) -> Optional[bytes]:
        try:
            with open(path, "rb") as f:
                return f.read()
        except Exception:
            return None

    def _save_bytes(self, path: str, data: bytes):
        self._ensure_dir()
        with open(path, "wb") as f:
            f.write(data)

    def _fetch_bin(self, url: str, meta_in: Dict, conditional=True) -> Tuple[bool, bytes, Dict]:
        headers = {}
        if conditional:
            if meta_in.get("etag"):
                headers["If-None-Match"] = meta_in["etag"]
            if meta_in.get("last_mod") or meta_in.get("last_modified"):
                headers["If-Modified-Since"] = meta_in.get("last_mod") or meta_in.get("last_modified")
        r = http_get(url, headers=headers, timeout=30)
        status = r.status_code
        return True, r.content, {
            "status": status,
            "etag": r.headers.get("ETag"),
            "last_mod": r.headers.get("Last-Modified"),
        }

    # -- public: ensure/clear bins --
    def ensure_t2sl(self, check_update=False, force_redownload=False) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        disk_meta = self._load_meta(META_T2SL) if self.persist else {}
        disk_bytes = self._load_bytes(FILE_T2SL) if self.persist else None

        need_fetch = force_redownload or (self.persist and not disk_bytes) or (not self.t2sl_loaded and not self.persist)
        if need_fetch:
            ok, data, hdr = self._fetch_bin(BIN_URL_T2SL, disk_meta, conditional=not force_redownload)
            if not ok:
                return False, "Download failed"
            if not data and disk_bytes:
                data = disk_bytes
            if not data:
                return False, "No data for T2SL"
            self.t2sl_bin.load_from_bytes(data)
            self.t2sl_loaded = True
            if self.persist:
                self._save_bytes(FILE_T2SL, data)
                meta = {
                    "ts": time.time(),
                    "v": self.t2sl_bin.meta.version,
                    "count": self.t2sl_bin.meta.count,
                    "blob_len": self.t2sl_bin.meta.blob_len,
                    "etag": hdr.get("etag"),
                    "last_mod": hdr.get("last_mod"),
                }
                self._save_meta(META_T2SL, meta)
            return True, "Loaded"

        if check_update and self.persist:
            ok, data, hdr = self._fetch_bin(BIN_URL_T2SL, disk_meta, conditional=True)
            if not ok:
                return False, "Update check failed"
            if data:
                self.t2sl_bin.load_from_bytes(data)
                self.t2sl_loaded = True
                self._save_bytes(FILE_T2SL, data)
                meta = {
                    "ts": time.time(),
                    "v": self.t2sl_bin.meta.version,
                    "count": self.t2sl_bin.meta.count,
                    "blob_len": self.t2sl_bin.meta.blob_len,
                    "etag": hdr.get("etag"),
                    "last_mod": hdr.get("last_mod"),
                }
                self._save_meta(META_T2SL, meta)
                return True, "Updated"
            return True, "Up to date (304?)"

        if self.persist and disk_bytes and not self.t2sl_loaded:
            self.t2sl_bin.load_from_bytes(disk_bytes)
            self.t2sl_loaded = True
            return True, "Loaded from disk"
        return (self.t2sl_loaded, "Already loaded" if self.t2sl_loaded else "Not loaded")

    def ensure_lbd(self, check_update=False, force_redownload=False) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        disk_meta = self._load_meta(META_LBD) if self.persist else {}
        disk_bytes = self._load_bytes(FILE_LBD) if self.persist else None

        need_fetch = force_redownload or (self.persist and not disk_bytes) or (not self.lbd_loaded and not self.persist)
        if need_fetch:
            ok, data, hdr = self._fetch_bin(BIN_URL_LBD, disk_meta, conditional=not force_redownload)
            if not ok:
                return False, "Download failed"
            if not data and disk_bytes:
                data = disk_bytes
            if not data:
                return False, "No data for LBD pairs"
            self.lbd_pairs.load_from_bytes(data)
            self.lbd_loaded = True
            if self.persist:
                self._save_bytes(FILE_LBD, data)
                meta = {
                    "ts": time.time(),
                    "count": self.lbd_pairs.meta.count,
                    "etag": hdr.get("etag"),
                    "last_mod": hdr.get("last_mod"),
                }
                self._save_meta(META_LBD, meta)
            return True, "Loaded"

        if check_update and self.persist:
            ok, data, hdr = self._fetch_bin(BIN_URL_LBD, disk_meta, conditional=True)
            if not ok:
                return False, "Update check failed"
            if data:
                self.lbd_pairs.load_from_bytes(data)
                self.lbd_loaded = True
                self._save_bytes(FILE_LBD, data)
                meta = {
                    "ts": time.time(),
                    "count": self.lbd_pairs.meta.count,
                    "etag": hdr.get("etag"),
                    "last_mod": hdr.get("last_mod"),
                }
                self._save_meta(META_LBD, meta)
                return True, "Updated"
            return True, "Up to date (304?)"

        if self.persist and disk_bytes and not self.lbd_loaded:
            self.lbd_pairs.load_from_bytes(disk_bytes)
            self.lbd_loaded = True
            return True, "Loaded from disk"
        return (self.lbd_loaded, "Already loaded" if self.lbd_loaded else "Not loaded")

    def clear_t2sl(self):
        self.t2sl_bin = T2SLBin(); self.t2sl_loaded = False
        if self.persist:
            for p in (FILE_T2SL, META_T2SL):
                try:
                    if os.path.exists(p):
                        os.remove(p)
                except Exception:
                    pass

    def clear_lbd(self):
        self.lbd_pairs = LBDPairs(); self.lbd_loaded = False
        if self.persist:
            for p in (FILE_LBD, META_LBD):
                try:
                    if os.path.exists(p):
                        os.remove(p)
                except Exception:
                    pass

def resolve_slug_via_redirect(tmdb_id: int) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Fallback if bin doesn't contain the entry.
    We follow https://letterboxd.com/tmdb/<id>/ redirect to /film/<slug>/
    """
    url = f"{LBX_ORIGIN}/tmdb/{tmdb_id}/"
    try:
        r = http_head(url, allow_redirects=True)
    except Exception:
        return None
    m = re.match(r"^https?://letterboxd\.com/film/([^/]+)/?$", r.url)
    return m.group(1) if m else None

def letterboxd_similar_url(slug: str) -> str:    return f"{LBX_ORIGIN}/film/{slug}/similar/"
def letterboxd_themes_url(slug: str) -> str:     return f"{LBX_ORIGIN}/film/{slug}/themes/"
def letterboxd_nano_url(slug: str) -> str:       return f"{LBX_ORIGIN}/film/{slug}/nanogenres/"

def to_ajax_url(listing_url: str, page: int) -> str:
    """
    Convert the visible listing URL to Letterboxd's internal AJAX URL for a page.

    FIXED/ROBUST:
      • Insert 'ajax' right after 'films' path segment (like your userscript).
      • Normalize '/page/<n>/' suffix.
      • Preserve existing query params AND force 'esiAllowFilters=true'.
    """
    pu = urlparse(listing_url)
    parts = [p for p in pu.path.split("/") if p]
    if "films" in parts:
        i = parts.index("films")
        if i + 1 >= len(parts) or parts[i + 1] != "ajax":
            parts.insert(i + 1, "ajax")
    path = "/" + "/".join(parts) + f"/page/{page}/"

    # Merge existing query params and add esiAllowFilters=true
    q_pairs = dict(parse_qsl(pu.query, keep_blank_values=True))
    q_pairs["esiAllowFilters"] = "true"
    query = urlencode(q_pairs, doseq=True)

    return urlunparse((pu.scheme, pu.netloc, path, "", query, ""))

def fetch_html(url: str) -> str:
    """
    One GET → text. We rely on requests' decoding (gzip → text).
    """
    return http_get(url).text

# ---------- attribute parsing helpers (robust to single/double quotes) ----------

_ATTR_RE_CACHE: Dict[str, re.Pattern] = {}
def _attr_re(name: str) -> re.Pattern:
    p = _ATTR_RE_CACHE.get(name)
    if p is None:
        # matches name="..." OR name='...'
        p = re.compile(r'(?i)\b' + re.escape(name) + r'\s*=\s*(?:"([^"]*)"|\'([^\']*)\')')
        _ATTR_RE_CACHE[name] = p
    return p

def _get_attr(source: str, name: str) -> Optional[str]:
    m = _attr_re(name).search(source)
    if not m:
        return None
    return m.group(1) if m.group(1) is not None else m.group(2)

_TAG_WITH_FILMID_RE = re.compile(
    r"<([a-zA-Z0-9:_-]+)([^>]*\bdata-film-id\s*=\s*(?:\"(\d+)\"|'(\d+)')[^>]*)>",
    re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL
)

def _decode_html_entities(s: str) -> str:
    import html
    return html.unescape(s or "")

def _strip_year_parens(name: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"\s*\(\d{4}\)\s*$", "", name or "").strip()

def extract_similar_from_html(html: str) -> List[Tuple[int, str]]:
    """
    BIG PICTURE:
      • We only need (filmId, display title).
      • This scans all tags containing data-film-id and pulls name from the most reliable attributes.

    FINE DETAIL:
      • Priority order (like your userscript):
         data-item-name > data-film-name > data-item-full-display-name > data-original-title > title > img alt
      • We dedupe by ID while preserving first-seen DOM order.
    """
    out: List[Tuple[int, str]] = []
    seen: set[int] = set()

    for m in _TAG_WITH_FILMID_RE.finditer(html):
        attr_chunk = m.group(2)
        film_id_str = m.group(3) or m.group(4)
        if not film_id_str:
            continue
        fid = int(film_id_str)
        if fid in seen:
            continue

        # Preferred attributes on *this* tag
        name = (
            _get_attr(attr_chunk, "data-item-name")
            or _get_attr(attr_chunk, "data-film-name")
            or _get_attr(attr_chunk, "data-item-full-display-name")
            or _get_attr(attr_chunk, "data-original-title")
            or _get_attr(attr_chunk, "title")
        )

        # Fallback: if this tag is an <img> or similar, its 'alt' might carry the name.
        if not name:
            name = _get_attr(attr_chunk, "alt")

        if not name:
            # As a last resort, peek a small window to the right for an <img alt="...">
            start = m.end()
            window = html[start:start + 300]
            name = _get_attr(window, "alt")

        # Normalize
        name = _strip_year_parens(_decode_html_entities(name or ""))

        seen.add(fid)
        out.append((fid, name))

    return out

# -- Groups (Themes/Nanogenres) --

_SECTION_RE = re.compile(
    r"<section[^>]*\bclass\s*=\s*(?:\"[^\"]*\bsection\b[^\"]*\bgenre-group\b[^\"]*\"|'[^']*\bsection\b[^']*\bgenre-group\b[^']*')[^>]*>(.*?)</section>",
    re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL
)
_H2_RE = re.compile(r"<h2[^>]*>(.*?)</h2>", re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
_A_IN_H2_RE = re.compile(r"<a[^>]*href\s*=\s*(?:\"([^\"]+)\"|'([^']+)')[^>]*>(.*?)</a>", re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
_LABEL_IN_H2_RE = re.compile(r"class\s*=\s*(?:\"[^\"]*\blabel\b[^\"]*\"|'[^']*\blabel\b[^']*')", re.IGNORECASE)

def extract_groups_from_html(html: str) -> List[Dict]:
    """
    BIG PICTURE:
      • Find each "genre-group" section.
      • For each, extract title + optional href.
      • Within the section, scan data-film-id items (same attribute strategy as 'similar').

    FINE DETAIL:
      • We keep DOM order by scanning in document order and dedup within each section.
    """
    groups: List[Dict] = []

    for sec_m in _SECTION_RE.finditer(html):
        block = sec_m.group(1) or ""

        # Extract heading (title + optional link href)
        title = ""
        href_abs = None
        h2m = _H2_RE.search(block)
        if h2m:
            h2_html = h2m.group(1) or ""
            linkm = _A_IN_H2_RE.search(h2_html)
            if linkm:
                href_rel = linkm.group(1) or linkm.group(2)
                title_text = (linkm.group(3) or "").strip()
                title = _decode_html_entities(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", title_text)).strip()
                if href_rel:
                    href_abs = urljoin(LBX_ORIGIN, href_rel)
            else:
                # Try a label span inside H2
                if _LABEL_IN_H2_RE.search(h2_html):
                    title_text = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", h2_html)
                    title = _decode_html_entities(title_text).strip()

        # Collect items inside the section block
        seen = set()
        items: List[Dict] = []
        for m in _TAG_WITH_FILMID_RE.finditer(block):
            film_id_str = m.group(3) or m.group(4)
            if not film_id_str:
                continue
            fid = int(film_id_str)
            if fid in seen:
                continue
            attr_chunk = m.group(2)
            name = (
                _get_attr(attr_chunk, "data-item-name")
                or _get_attr(attr_chunk, "data-film-name")
                or _get_attr(attr_chunk, "data-item-full-display-name")
                or _get_attr(attr_chunk, "data-original-title")
                or _get_attr(attr_chunk, "title")
                or _get_attr(attr_chunk, "alt")
            )
            if not name:
                # Small lookahead window for <img alt="...">
                start = m.end()
                window = block[start:start + 300]
                name = _get_attr(window, "alt")
            name = _strip_year_parens(_decode_html_entities(name or ""))
            seen.add(fid)
            items.append({"id": fid, "name": name})

        if title and items:
            groups.append({"title": title, "href": href_abs, "items": items})

    return groups

# ---------- FIXED PAGINATION DETECTION (more tolerant) ----------

# Matches an <a ... class="... next ..."> anchor (any order/case/quotes).
_NEXT_ANCHOR_RE = re.compile(
    r"<a\b[^>]*\bclass\s*=\s*(?:\"[^\"]*\bnext\b[^\"]*\"|'[^']*\bnext\b[^']*')[^>]*>",
    re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL
)
# Matches an <a ... class="... previous ..."> or <a ... class="... prev ..."> anchor.
_PREV_ANCHOR_RE = re.compile(
    r"<a\b[^>]*\bclass\s*=\s*(?:\"[^\"]*\b(?:previous|prev)\b[^\"]*\"|'[^']*\b(?:previous|prev)\b[^']*')[^>]*>",
    re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL
)

def extract_ajax_tiles_from_html(html: str) -> Tuple[List[Tuple[int, str]], bool, bool]:
    """
    Extract the tile list for AJAX pages plus pagination flags.

    WHAT WAS WRONG BEFORE (and why this fixes it):
    ----------------------------------------------
    • We used to look for a very specific wrapper: <div class="pagination"> ... </div>.
      On some LBX AJAX responses, the pagination is not a <div>, or it appears outside
      the exact subtree we scanned. That made us miss the presence of a “Next” link.
    • Now we scan the entire fragment for ANY <a> with class .next for forward paging,
      and .previous/.prev for backwards—matching your userscript's effective logic.

    We still try to limit tile scanning to the poster list block to avoid noise.
    """
    # Limit the tile scan to the poster-list block if present
    ul_match = re.search(
        r"<ul[^>]*\bclass\s*=\s*(?:\"[^\"]*\bposter-list\b[^\"]*\"|'[^']*\bposter-list\b[^']*')[^>]*>(.*?)</ul>",
        html, re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL
    )
    block = ul_match.group(1) if ul_match else html

    rows = extract_similar_from_html(block)

    # NEW: Robust pagination detection on the whole HTML fragment
    has_next = bool(_NEXT_ANCHOR_RE.search(html))
    has_prev = bool(_PREV_ANCHOR_RE.search(html))

    return rows, has_next, has_prev

class LBXEngine:
    """
    Public API for the add-on code (or for this demo GUI):

      • resolve_slug(tmdb_id, media, tmdb_title) -> (slug, via)
      • get_similar(tmdb_id, media, tmdb_title)  -> payload with rows mapped to TMDb
      • get_groups(kind, ...)                    -> Themes/Nanogenres groups + mapped items
      • get_group_page(listing_url, page, ctx)   -> AJAX pagination

    'media' is "movie" or "tv". All returned rows include TMDb ID if present in the LBD cache.
    """
    def __init__(self, cache: "CacheManager") -> None:
        self.cache = cache

    def resolve_slug(self, tmdb_id: int, media: str, tmdb_title: str) -> Tuple[str, str]:
        # First, try local bin (fast path; no network).
        slug, via = self.cache.t2sl_bin.resolve_slug(tmdb_id, media, tmdb_title)
        if slug:
            return slug, via
        # Fallback: one HEAD redirect to the canonical film slug.
        slug = resolve_slug_via_redirect(tmdb_id)
        return (slug, "letterboxd-resolver" if slug else "none")

    def _map_rows(self, rows: List[Tuple[int, str]]):
        """
        Map Letterboxd film IDs → TMDb IDs using our in-RAM u32 pairs.
        This is O(log N) per row and typically < 1 ms total for page 1 sizes.
        """
        t0 = time.time()
        mapped = []
        matched = 0
        for fid, name in rows:
            m = self.cache.lbd_pairs.lookup(fid)
            if m:
                tmdb_id, is_tv = m
                mapped.append((fid, name, tmdb_id, 1 if is_tv else 0))
                matched += 1
            else:
                mapped.append((fid, name, None, 0))
        return mapped, matched, len(rows) - matched, int((time.time() - t0) * 1000)

    def get_similar(self, tmdb_id: int, media: str, tmdb_title: str):
        t0 = time.time()
        slug, via = self.resolve_slug(tmdb_id, media, tmdb_title)
        if not slug:
            raise RuntimeError("Could not resolve Letterboxd slug.")
        html = fetch_html(letterboxd_similar_url(slug))
        rows = extract_similar_from_html(html)
        mapped, matched, unmatched, ms_map = self._map_rows(rows)
        return {
            "slug": slug, "via": via, "rows": mapped,
            "matched": matched, "unmatched": unmatched,
            "ms_map": ms_map, "ms_total": int((time.time() - t0) * 1000),
        }

    def get_groups(self, kind: str, tmdb_id: int, media: str, tmdb_title: str):
        t0 = time.time()
        slug, via = self.resolve_slug(tmdb_id, media, tmdb_title)
        if not slug:
            raise RuntimeError("Could not resolve Letterboxd slug.")
        url = letterboxd_themes_url(slug) if kind == "themes" else letterboxd_nano_url(slug)
        html = fetch_html(url)
        groups0 = extract_groups_from_html(html)

        matched_total = 0
        unmatched_total = 0
        t_map0 = time.time()
        groups = []
        for g in groups0:
            mapped, matched, unmatched, _ = self._map_rows([(it["id"], it["name"]) for it in g["items"]])
            matched_total += matched
            unmatched_total += unmatched
            groups.append({
                "title": g["title"],
                "href": g["href"],
                "items": [{"id": fid, "name": nm, "tmdb_id": tmdb, "is_tv": is_tv} for fid, nm, tmdb, is_tv in mapped],
            })
        return {
            "slug": slug, "via": via, "groups": groups,
            "matched": matched_total, "unmatched": unmatched_total,
            "ms_map": int((time.time() - t_map0) * 1000),
            "ms_total": int((time.time() - t0) * 1000),
        }

    def get_group_page(self, listing_url: str, page: int, ctx: Dict):
        t0 = time.time()
        ajax = to_ajax_url(listing_url, page)
        html = fetch_html(ajax)
        rows, has_next, has_prev = extract_ajax_tiles_from_html(html)
        mapped, matched, unmatched, ms_map = self._map_rows(rows)
        return {
            "page": page,
            "rows": [{"id": fid, "name": nm, "tmdb_id": tmdb, "is_tv": is_tv} for fid, nm, tmdb, is_tv in mapped],
            "has_next": has_next, "has_prev": has_prev,
            "matched": matched, "unmatched": unmatched,
            "ms_map": ms_map, "ms_total": int((time.time() - t0) * 1000),
            "slug": ctx.get("slug"), "via": ctx.get("via"),
        }

# OPTIONAL: URL → TMDb media/id/title parser (for GUI convenience/demo)
# =============================================================================

def parse_tmdb_from_url(url: str) -> Tuple[Optional[str], Optional[int], Optional[str]]:
    """
    Given a TMDb title URL, try to parse media + id + title (title via og:title).
    """
    m = re.search(r"https?://www\.themoviedb\.org/(movie|tv)/(\d+)(?:-[^/?#]*)?", url)
    if not m:
        return None, None, None
    media = m.group(1); tmdb_id = int(m.group(2))
    title = None
    try:
        html = fetch_html(url)
        mt = re.search(r'<meta property="og:title" content="([^"]+)"', html)
        if mt:
            title = mt.group(1).strip()
        else:
            t2 = re.search(r"<title>(.*?)</title>", html, flags=re.I | re.S)
            if t2:
                title = t2.group(1).split("—", 1)[0].trim()
    except Exception:
        pass
    return media, tmdb_id, title

            step = -1 if event.delta > 0 else 1
            self.grp_canvas.yview_scroll(step, "units")

        for child in self.stack.winfo_children():
            child.pack_forget()
        if name == "similar":
            self.similar_frame.pack(fill="both", expand=True)
        else:
            self.groups_frame.pack(fill="both", expand=True)

    def set_status(self, msg: str):
        self.status.set(msg); self.update_idletasks()

    def get_input_tuple(self) -> Tuple[str, int, str]:
        mode = self.use_mode_var.get()
        if mode == "url":
            url = self.tmdb_url_entry.get().strip()
            media, tmdb_id, title = parse_tmdb_from_url(url) if url else (None, None, None)
            if not media or not tmdb_id:
                raise ValueError("Could not parse TMDb media/id from URL.")
            if not title:
                title = self.tmdb_title_entry.get().strip() or ""
            return media, tmdb_id, title
        else:
            media = self.media_var.get().strip()
            try:
                tmdb_id = int(self.tmdb_id_entry.get().strip())
            except Exception:
                raise ValueError("TMDb ID is required (integer).")
            title = self.tmdb_title_entry.get().strip()
            if not title:
                raise ValueError("TMDb Title is required.")
            return media, tmdb_id, title

    def ensure_bins(self):
        self.cache.persist = self.persist_var.get()
        ok1, msg1 = self.cache.ensure_t2sl(force_redownload=False)
        ok2, msg2 = self.cache.ensure_lbd(force_redownload=False)
        if not ok1 or not ok2:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Bin load failed: T2SL={msg1}, LBD={msg2}")

    def _copy_similar_csv(self):
        rows = []
        for iid in self.items_tree.get_children():
            lbx_id, title, tmdb_id, is_tv = self.items_tree.item(iid, "values")
            t = str(title).replace('"', '""')
            rows.append(f'{lbx_id},"{t}",{"" if tmdb_id=="" else tmdb_id},{is_tv}')
        csv = "lbx_id,name,tmdb_id,is_tv\n" + "\n".join(rows)
        try:
            self.clipboard_clear(); self.clipboard_append(csv)
            messagebox.showinfo("Copied", "Similar CSV copied to clipboard.", parent=self)
        except Exception:
            messagebox.showerror("Error", "Could not copy to clipboard.", parent=self)

    def on_similar(self):
        def work():
            try:
                self.set_status("Loading bins…")
                self.ensure_bins()
                media, tmdb_id, title = self.get_input_tuple()
                self.set_status("Resolving slug & fetching Similar…")
                res = self.engine.get_similar(tmdb_id, media, title)
                self._show_frame("similar")
                self.items_tree.delete(*self.items_tree.get_children())
                for fid, name, tmdb_id2, is_tv in res["rows"]:
                    self.items_tree.insert("", "end", values=(fid, name, "" if tmdb_id2 is None else tmdb_id2, is_tv))
                self.sim_summary.set(
                    f"TMDb: {media}/{tmdb_id} • Slug: {res['slug']} ({res['via']}) • "
                    f"Items: {len(res['rows'])} • Matched: {res['matched']} • Missing: {res['unmatched']} • "
                    f"Elapsed: {res['ms_total']} ms (map {res['ms_map']} ms)"
                )
                self.set_status("Done.")
            except Exception as e:
                messagebox.showerror("Error", str(e), parent=self); self.set_status("Error.")
        threading.Thread(target=work, daemon=True).start()

    def on_open_similar(self):
        try:
            self.ensure_bins()

class GroupPopup(tk.Toplevel):  # type: ignore[misc]
    """
    Simple popup to mirror your AJAX paginated list: Prev/Next + CSV.

    IMPORTANT (re: the bug you saw):
      • The 'Next' button’s enabled/disabled state is now driven by the more tolerant
        pagination detection in extract_ajax_tiles_from_html(), so it reflects LBX correctly.
    """
    def __init__(self, parent: App, engine: LBXEngine, title: str, href: str, ctx: Dict):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.title(f"{title} — Letterboxd Group")
        self.geometry("860x620")
        self.engine = engine
        self.href = href
        self.ctx = ctx
        self.page_cache: Dict[int, Dict] = {}
        self.current_page = 1
        self.group_title = title

        frm = tk.Frame(self, bg="#1e1f24"); frm.pack(fill="both", expand=True)
        self.summary = tk.StringVar(value="")
        tk.Label(frm, textvariable=self.summary, bg="#1e1f24", fg="#e9e9ef",
                 anchor="w", font=("Segoe UI", 10, "bold")).pack(fill="x", padx=8, pady=(8, 4))

        cols = ("lbx_id", "title", "tmdb_id", "is_tv")
        self.tree = ttk.Treeview(frm, columns=cols, show="headings", height=22)
        for c, w in zip(cols, (140, 460, 140, 80)):
            self.tree.heading(c, text=c)
            self.tree.column(c, width=w, anchor="w")
        self.tree.pack(fill="both", expand=True, padx=8, pady=(0, 6))

        bar = ttk.Frame(frm); bar.pack(fill="x", padx=8, pady=8)
        self.btn_copy = ttk.Button(bar, text="Copy CSV", command=self.copy_csv)
        self.btn_prev = ttk.Button(bar, text="◀ Prev", command=self.prev_page)
        self.btn_next = ttk.Button(bar, text="Next ▶", command=self.next_page)
        self.btn_close = ttk.Button(bar, text="Close", command=self.destroy)
        self.btn_copy.pack(side="left")
        self.btn_close.pack(side="right")
        self.btn_next.pack(side="right", padx=6)
        self.btn_prev.pack(side="right")

        self.render(1)

    def fetch_page(self, page: int) -> Dict:
        if page in self.page_cache:
            return self.page_cache[page]
        data = self.engine.get_group_page(self.href, page, {"slug": self.ctx.get("slug"), "via": self.ctx.get("via")})
        self.page_cache[page] = data
        return data

    def render(self, page: int):
        data = self.fetch_page(page)
        self.tree.delete(*self.tree.get_children())
        for r in data["rows"]:
            self.tree.insert("", "end", values=(r["id"], r["name"], "" if r["tmdb_id"] is None else r["tmdb_id"], r["is_tv"]))
        self.summary.set(
            f"{self.group_title} • Slug: {data['slug']} ({data['via']}) • "
            f"Page: {page} • Items: {len(data['rows'])} • Matched: {data['matched']} • "
            f"Elapsed: {data['ms_total']} ms (map {data['ms_map']} ms)"
        )
        self.current_page = page
        self.btn_prev.state(("!disabled",) if (data.get("has_prev") or page > 1) else ("disabled",))
        self.btn_next.state(("!disabled",) if data.get("has_next") else ("disabled",))

    def prev_page(self):
        target = max(1, self.current_page - 1)
        if target != self.current_page:
            self.render(target)

    def next_page(self):
        data = self.fetch_page(self.current_page)
        if data.get("has_next"):
            self.render(self.current_page + 1)

    def copy_csv(self):
        rows = []
        for iid in self.tree.get_children():
            lbx_id, title, tmdb_id, is_tv = self.tree.item(iid, "values")
            t = str(title).replace('"', '""')
            rows.append(f'{lbx_id},"{t}",{"" if tmdb_id=="" else tmdb_id},{is_tv}')
        csv = "lbx_id,name,tmdb_id,is_tv\n" + "\n".join(rows)
        try:
            self.clipboard_clear(); self.clipboard_append(csv)
            messagebox.showinfo("Copied", "CSV copied to clipboard.", parent=self)
        except Exception:
            messagebox.showerror("Error", "Could not copy to clipboard.", parent=self)
